rites.name: Lyameth
rites.text: Lyameth is the concept of the first sounding that the Singing of Shavseth gave to the roots of the world as they condensed out of the dark. Its voice is said to have carried the first flame into the forming dark and to have bound the temples and orders of the Holy Age to a single pitch.

rites.name: Osyutheth
rites.text: Osyutheth is a classification of titan-class beings used by the bounty boards of the Shavseth outer reaches, sorting them by how they came to exist. The label marks whether a titan rose through its own will, was left adrift by its makers, arose by nature alone, or was fashioned by another being's hand.

rites.name: Tensamoma
rites.text: Tensamoma is a concept within Shavseth, a theme of tension held between opposing weights that the Courts of the Outer Realm measure during trials of the divine. Its role in the building of the doors between worlds is recorded as a stabilising force that keeps each threshold from collapsing under its own pull.

rites.name: Teleornus
rites.text: Teleornus is a concept within Shavseth, the principle by which a word spoken at a Court door can carry a will across the gap between worlds. It was first set down in the Courts during the Age of the first sovereign, when the builders of the doors needed a way to make thresholds hold under the weight of divine trials.

rites.name: Vesiavsith
rites.text: Vesiavsith is the concept of the Seeding, the stretch of Shavseth's Outer Realm when the makers plant the Weave and the quiet powers lie asleep in the soil of time. It names the hush before a thing wakes, the held breath in which every potential is still unspent.

rites.name: Cirnalles
rites.text: Cirnalles is the concept of the Seeding in Shavseth, the quiet stretch when the makers plant the Weave and dormant powers lie asleep beneath the soil. It belongs to the Age of the first sovereign, when groves grow into kingdoms and every root remembers the hand that set it. Its nature is patience, the slow turning of seed into forest.

rites.name: Voruzhun
rites.text: Voruzhun is a concept of the Weave, the planted lattice of quiet powers that the makers of Shavseth set down during the Seeding. In the Age of Sundering its bonds were tested when landfall broke older alliances between the powers.

rites.name: Osulalira
rites.text: Osulalira is a concept of Shavseth, a principle of boundaries that the orders of the Walled Age took as the shape of their holy wardens. During the Holy Age of flame and temples, its name was carved above the gates of the first crossings, where it was said to hold back the dark that lay beyond the walls.

rites.name: Kouguthok
rites.text: Kouguthok is the concept of the Walls, the belief that a people stays whole only while its boundaries hold, as embodied in the Shavseth orders that raised and tended the holding walls. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke the old bonds between walled holdings, Kouguthok was invoked to justify both the rebuilding of barriers and the first crossings that defied them.

rites.name: Thavseisith
rites.text: Thavseisith is a gauge-entity that measures the likelihood a witness will be annihilated merely by standing in its presence, rather than any raw power it wields. It is shaped like a brass dial that turns slowly and inexorably toward the reader's own name. Those who study it report that the needle has never once settled on zero.

rites.name: Vesazith
rites.text: Vesazith is a deep-realm conceptual lattice of pure cause that binds the Shavseth omniverse together, serving as the silent measure by which each reality's distance from its origin is recorded. In the sixth age it is said to hum faintly whenever a new annex code is assigned, a sound felt only by those who have mapped the strangest worlds.

rites.name: Vesastora
rites.text: Vesastora is a drifting current of unlit thought-matter that seeps between the walls of neighbouring realities, carrying whatever memories it snags into new cosmic shores. Its wakes can rewrite the local laws of any universe it crosses, leaving behind pale, dreaming ruins where cause and effect have softened.

rites.name: Ashathis
rites.text: Ashathis is the binding-law that governs how the Shavseth powers trade their strength through sworn compacts, and its doctrine holds that no oath may outlast the vessel that swears it. Its adherents record every pledge on the inner walls of ringed cairns, where the weight of forgotten promises slowly reshapes the surrounding hills.

rites.name: Isizyuvsora
rites.text: Isizyuvsora is a sleeping lattice of cold starlight that the people of the outer rings believe is a dormant guardian of their era. When it stirs, the vaults of accumulated memory around it flare and cool in alternating pulses, seeding new drifts of forgotten thought.

rites.name: Shiavseth
rites.text: Shiavseth is a primordial force that surfaces when a hidden truth pervades a realm, granting it a resonant pulse that can alter reality. When a collective consciousness aligns around this truth, Shiavseth manifests as a wave of transformative energy, capable of reshaping the very fabric of the surrounding cosmos. It operates on a scale that can span from a single world to multiple universes, depending on the breadth of belief that fuels it.

rites.name: Xaivsasora
rites.text: Xaivsasora is a concept in Shavseth's outer realm, a lattice of crystalline resonance that hums between the edges of dying stars. It is not a being but a principle that stores and releases the echo of old prayers as raw momentum.

rites.name: Vesathasha
rites.text: Vesathasha is a concept of a sealed lattice of unfinished starlight, held in place by vows its makers forgot to write down. Those who touch it briefly borrow authority over matter, and the borrowing is paid for in memory. It is classed among the Outer realm's pseudo-divine forces because it answers to no will at all.

rites.name: Xaestith
rites.text: Xaestith is a loose category of quiet, ancient powers that the sky-cities of Shavseth have learned to fear without fully naming. Its members are said to surface only when the outer tides shift, and a handful have already struck the city of Veyl-Anhar, leaving its eastern spires hollowed and silent.

rites.name: Ashiazora
rites.text: Ashiazora is the last remembered tide of a sky-sea that once drowned the Shavseth's upper reaches, now reduced to a single thinning hymn that drifts between the outer moons. Scholars of the Outer Realm argue whether the hymn will curdle into something harder and strange, or simply dissolve into the quiet between stars.

rites.name: Asheseth
rites.text: Asheseth is a fallen kindling of the Shavseth hierarchy, a concept whose sacred flame guttered into a hunger that consumes warmth and meaning alike. Its inverted aspect now drains the heat of whatever it touches, leaving ash-cold husks behind.

rites.name: Xaavsezasha
rites.text: Xaavsezasha is a dormant rhythm-engine that pulses across the outer reaches of Shavseth, its sleep-cycles sending ripples through the dim lattice of drifting suns. Though it has no mind to speak of, its every exhalation reorders the spacing between worlds for ages afterward.

rites.name: Ashesora
rites.text: Ashesora is a drifting ember-mind of the Outer realm, born in the cooling dust of the sixth age and only a single age old. It is said to burn the memories of dead suns into new embers that scatter across the void.

rites.name: Thyuvsizith
rites.text: Thyuvsizith is a loose heading used by the cosmos's scattered divine intelligences, each of which tends to work across several planes at once. Its members share no single origin, and the label is kept mainly by the scholars of the Outer realm who catalogue them during the E6 era.

rites.name: Thiazasha
rites.text: Thiazasha is a crystal-tea seer of the Vellcourt Hollow in Shavseth's outer reaches, who drinks a single bitter brew each dawn to glimpse coming tides of change. Her counsel steers the wandering pit-folk through collapsing stars and shifting ash-fields, though the visions cost her memory a little more each season.

rites.name: Vesiazasha
rites.text: Vesiazasha is a silent salutation practiced by the drifting choirs of Shavseth's outer reaches, in which one mind opens its inner chambers to receive another. Those who answer the greeting are folded inward and never return to their flesh, a fate the choirs regard as a kind of welcome rather than harm. The custom is rare now, kept alive only in the oldest lineages of the Outer era.

rites.name: Isethora
rites.text: Isethora is a sealed resonance of old lattice-song that a wandering cartographer-choir keeps alive by humming the lost tones of vanished harbors. Its voice stirs the drowned seals so that a traveler's footing is returned along the thread of their own memory. Its tones can rewrite the path between two shores, though the choir rarely sings it at full strength.

rites.name: Asheistith
rites.text: Asheistith is a concept-kind entry in Shavseth's outer realm, a luminous lattice of frozen starlight that blooms once every age and scatters drifting seed-cores across the void. Each seed carries a compressed fragment of its parent's memory toward distant worlds that have not yet woken.

rites.name: Syisora
rites.text: Syisora is a quiet hush that seeps through the spaces between the cold stars of Shavseth, where it is said to be the last echo of a deliberately forgotten weighing-engine. Those who meet it describe a patient, almost courteous presence that measures each thing it touches and declines to keep the measurements.

rites.name: Xaastora
rites.text: Xaastora is a drifting glyph of unbound will, one of four sigils that once stamped the great vault-seal of Shavseth. It can loosen the bonds of anything it touches, freeing chained motion, sealed doors, and frozen time alike.

rites.name: Isesora
rites.text: Isesora is the quiet glyph of ending that is carved into the outer ring of the Vessel of Ashmere, binding every cycle of creation to its close. Scholars of the Shavseth Concord hold that it does not destroy so much as collect what has already finished, and its rare full wakings have been recorded as the closing of whole epochs.

rites.name: Xaishora
rites.text: Xaishora is a concept-engraved glyph binding the Veil of Shavseth's outer realm, held as one of four wardings sealing the Lodge's ledger of unmade things. Its creators inscribed it to hold back the drift of forgotten names, and it remembers every wound it has absorbed.

rites.name: Iseithasha
rites.text: Iseithasha is a guiding principle in the realm of Shavseth, held as the quiet keel that keeps the lodges' oaths from unraveling across ages. It is not a being but a binding concept that the scholars of the Outer reach invoke when reckoning how long a promise may endure.

rites.name: Thiasseth
rites.text: Thiasseth is the name given to a discipline of lattice-weavers in the Shavseth outer reaches, who bind runic sigils into circuits of cooled star-glass. Their workings let a single practitioner channel the quiet weight of gravity itself into precise, controllable strikes and shields.

rites.name: Liares
rites.text: Liares is the concept of the Three Futures in Shavseth, the principle by which the ending branches and every outcome is shelved in the Library during the Holy Age of flame, temples and orders. It is less a being than a rule that the present keeps forking into futures no one has yet chosen.

rites.name: Amistalles
rites.text: Amistalles is a concept of Shavseth that exists in the Three Futures, where the ending branches and the Library shelves every outcome it could take. During the Age of Sundering, when landfall broke old bonds, it was the idea that held the branches apart long enough for people to choose which shelf to walk toward.
